Reduced GAD67 function decreases basal GABA synthesis. GAD65 supplies residual and compartment-specific GABA but does not restore the normal cortical pool in null mice.
Reduced GABA availability disrupts network excitation-inhibition balance. GABA also has developmental signaling roles, so this does not imply that every fetal or neonatal action is inhibitory.
Loss of GABA signaling in the developing CNS impairs the fetal motor activity required for normal extra-neural morphogenesis.

GABA-dependent neural development is proposed to be impaired independently of ongoing seizures. Developmental deficits persisted after seizure freedom in several patients, although earlier seizure injury and direct developmental effects cannot be quantitatively separated.
Constitutive GABA deficiency is proposed to impair axial motor development; the authors make this interpretation specifically for axial hypotonia.
Reduced GABAergic restraint promotes network hyperexcitability; the exact developmental and regional intermediates in human DEE89 are unresolved.
Abnormal synchronized network discharge produces the clinical seizures, which begin neonatally or later in infancy.

Frequent early epileptic activity may add to the developmental deficit. The authors distinguish this potentially modifiable component from the prenatal developmental role of GABA; their relative contributions remain unresolved.

edges.description: GAD1 loss in the rat produces a hypersynchronous electrographic phenotype, supporting the general link from GABA synthesis failure to network hypersynchrony.
edges.limitations: The discharge type is absence-like spike-wave activity in adolescent and adult animals, mechanistically a thalamocortical oscillation, rather than the neonatal epileptic spasms and suppression-burst background that define the human disease. Common laboratory rat strains also show spike-wave discharges spontaneously, so the phenotype is a shift in severity against a noisy background rather than an all-or-none disease model. Valproate, which suppressed discharges in controls, made them worse in the nulls, so drug responses in this model should not be transferred to patients.

nodes.description:
Vigabatrin irreversibly inhibits GABA transaminase, the enzyme that degrades GABA, and is therefore a mechanistically rational attempt to raise whatever GABA the residual synthetic capacity produces. Five of seven patients in the founding cohort who tried it had a good seizure response, but the authors themselves cautioned that the responders were particularly those with epileptic spasms, so the effect may be semiology-driven rather than GAD1-specific.
The rationale has a published objection, and it is a mechanistic one rather than a null trial result: sparing GABA from degradation cannot help much when synthesis is the step that has failed, since GAD67 supplies over 90% of basal GABA. The 2023 review states that vigabatrin is therefore not a suitable solution "at least for mutations that result in severe reduction or complete loss of the enzyme function" - a genotype-stratified claim, which is the same residual-activity axis this entry records as an open gap. Two treated patients, including one on the vigabatrin-plus-ketogenic-diet combination, continued to have seizures. Both sides are curated as evidence below rather than resolved here, because the objection is an inference from the mechanism and the response is an observation, and neither refutes the other.
